artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $f_1,\dots,f_n:M\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth functions whose Hamiltonian vector fields pairwise Poisson-commute and are linearly independent almost everywhere, so that $(M,\omega,f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is a classical integrable system. Suppose this system is quantized by an $n$-tuple of pairwise commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ (e.g. $\hbar$-pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz operators) whose principal symbols are $f_1,\dots,f_n$. The semiclassical joint spectrum is the family, indexed by $\hbar\to 0$, of joint eigenvalues
$$\mathrm{JointSpec}(T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar})=\{(\lambda_1(\hbar),\dots,\lambda_n(\hbar))\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,v\neq 0,\ T_{j,\hbar}v=\lambda_j(\hbar)v\ \forall j\}.$$

A symplectic invariant of $(M,\omega,f_1,\dots,f_n)$ is any quantity (e.g. an integer, a polygon, a matrix, a Taylor series) that depends only on the equivalence class of the system under symplectomorphisms intertwining the momentum maps up to allowed transformations.

Problem. Determine which information about the principal symbols $f_1,\dots,f_n$ can be recovered from the semiclassical joint spectrum of $T_{1,\hbar},\dots,T_{n,\hbar}$ as $\hbar\to 0$. More precisely: given a symplectic invariant of $(M,\omega,f_1,\dots,f_n)$ (such as a specific integer $z$ or matrix $A$), produce an explicit algorithm that computes this invariant from the semiclassical joint spectrum.
artifact.category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for quantum integrable systems
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made in the semitoric case: Le Floch and Pelayo, together with related work by Pelayo–Vũ Ngọc, have shown that for (simple, and later non-simple) semitoric systems one can recover a complete set of symplectic invariants—and hence the system up to symplectic equivalence—from the semiclassical joint spectrum. The general problem for arbitrary finite-dimensional quantum integrable systems remains open beyond these classes.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic invariants of semitoric systems and the inverse problem for quantum systems
status_evidence.snippet: From the quantum spectrum in the semiclassical limit, one may extract a complete set of symplectic invariants in a constructive way.
status_evidence.claim: Inverse problem solved constructively for simple semitoric systems.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recovers the classical semitoric system from the semiclassical joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Partial solution extended to broader semitoric setting.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical inverse spectral theory for singularities of focus-focus type
status_evidence.snippet: Joint spectrum near a focus-focus critical value determines the classical Lagrangian foliation around the focus-focus leaf.
status_evidence.claim: Local recovery near focus-focus singularities established.
